openers.t: Name thine enemies, and I shall insult them, from a distance.
Swoon leftward, should thou swoon, for that is where I stand.
{wins} wins in {played} tourneys, which in Roman numerals looketh enormous.
Is thy little lit slate painting me, and from which side?
Behold the last of the great knights, the others having been sensible.
The post of muse is thine, fair one, and payeth in exposure.

q-first-date.t: To the pillory, where I have engaged a knave, at some expense, for thee to pelt with turnips.
A tour of mine ancestral castle, and if they ask, I am not with the coach party.

q-worst-habit.t: I correct everyone's Latin, loudly, at table, including people who were speaking French.
I duel all who mispronounce thy name, which hath, alas, twice included thee.

q-why-you.t: Why I, of all who stand before thee, plumed and polished, hopeful, glinting in the lamplight? Height.
These three would love thee for a season, whereas I would have thee bound in calfskin and shelved forever.

q-cut-who.t: Cut whichever of them hath a coach, but not until after he hath driven me home.
Whoever calleth thee cute, a word for lambs, when thou art plainly the Great Fire of London.

q-bad-mood.t: Pray be foul by the window, in profile, and hold it there whilst I find my pencil.
I summon the barber to bleed thee, as physic requireth, and since he is there, a fringe.

q-expensive.t: By patronage, so dost thou know a duke who wanteth a sonnet on his horse, or any horse?
Easily. My helm alone cost a fortune, from the finest bucket maker in Kent.

q-last-breakup.t: She was a milkmaid in a pastoral. She left the pastoral. I am still standing in the field.
My horse, who bore me through eleven battles, and now, I am told, belongeth to a nicer man.

q-fight.t: Thou art correct, and I shall die of it.
A preamble, setting forth our quarrel from the Norman Conquest onward, then, time permitting, sorry.

q-gift.t: A silver skull upon a ribbon, that thou mayest think on death daily, and on me, who bought it.
An acrostic sonnet with thy name running down the side, so pray tell me thy name is long.

q-describe-me.t: Sit for me a twelvemonth, for ninety seconds hath got me only as far as thine eyebrows.
Thou art a rose. I know not what thou art.

q-one-year.t: Wed, by a parson some years dead, irregular, I grant, but he was free.
In Venice, upon a gondola, thou rowing and I reciting, until one of us learneth to swim.

q-secret.t: I am of royal blood, on the evidence of my chin, and nobody else's.
Swear first upon thy mother's grave, or, she being alive, upon her hat.

star.t: Thou black eye upon the wall, art thou getting this, and is it in colour?
{star} hath not asked my full name, wisely, it having eleven parts and a motto.
{star} hath looked at me thrice tonight, and in my family that is an engagement.

rival.t: {rival} is no threat, as I have told {star} four times now, to be safe.
I would challenge {rival}, but {rival} hath the look of one who would come.
{rival} hath the bearing of a footman, and I would know, having been mistaken for one.

afterCringe.t: A wince. I have been winced at by a queen.
The king made that face at my recital, and knighted me to send me somewhere far away.

afterCharm.t: {star} smiled at me, and I have already sent the mason the measurements, rounded up.
By tourney law {star} now oweth me a favour, and I brought one along to save time.

final.t: {rival} would make {star} a lovely first husband.
I have drawn up {rival}'s elegy in advance, as a courtesy, with a space for the dates.
Should {star} pick {rival}, I retire to a monastery, and the monastery hath asked me not to.

guess.t: {star} liketh {card}, so fetch me {card}, and show me which end to hold.
{star} glanced at my sword, which can only mean {card}, and also, I suspect, the sword.
If {star} craveth {card}, then, viewed through a keyhole at dusk, {star} craveth me.
It is {card}, I would stake my horse on it, and indeed I already have.
Plainly {card}, and my tailor shall cut me a doublet of {card} by morning.
My guess is {card}, sealed in wax, to be opened only once I am proved right.

fear.t: At {card}, {star} shied like a horse from a pistol, and I am holding the pistol.
{card} offendeth {star}, and I, who invented {card}, hereby disown it.
{star} loathes {card}, so I have struck it from the ode, which is now a title.
{star} cannot abide {card}, and I shall give it up, along with everything I said tonight.

worst-trait.t: I forgive no slight to thee or me, and I have kept a book of them, with an index.
My worst trait is that I outlive everyone, chiefly by arriving at battles somewhat late.

ex-calls.t: Speak on, sir or madam or thing, and slowly, I am writing down what {star} hated.
I would strike thee with my glove, wert thou anywhere at all.
Peace, thou bygone voice, {star} hath moved on, to a knight with land, some of it dry.

rhyme.t: Choose me, fair one, and I shall be thy knight, for of these four I am the most upright.
Choose me, and all thy virtues I shall prove. In sixteen hundred, that rhymed with love.
I would swim the moat for thee in all my plate, so, fair one, bring a rope, and wait.

truth-lie.t: I have fought forty duels. I have lost none. Thou art welcome to inspect my wounds.
I have slain a dragon, and geese affright me, and whilst thou guessest, stand between me and that pond.

apology.t: Forgive me, beforehand, for the night I compare thee to the moon and thou noticest I mean the craters.
Pardon, in advance, the supper at which I recite to thy friends, standing, until they climb out the window.

budget-date.t: Keep thy five green portraits of a stranger, and come picnic where they used to hang people.
No invisible postman, so we shall court properly, by letters passed through a hedge.

logs.t: My chronicle recordeth that I have swooned at every sonnet I ever heard, chiefly mine.
I challenged the little red clerk who underlineth my words to a duel. He underlined the challenge.

impression.t: Sir Quill, I beg thee, read it again, the bit about my nose, which I adored.
Hush, every one of you, the knight is clearing his throat, and I have waited all my life.

parent.t: Most stern and humming mother of my muse, mine intentions are honourable, and in Latin.
Madam of a thousand copper roads, I ask thy child's hand, or whatever thy child hath instead of one.

dash.t: Dash courteth like a mountebank selling two cures for the same plague, and asketh the corpse which it preferred.

tilly.t: Tilly is less a lady than an apology that someone hath watered.

prince.t: A true nobleman, Prince, asketh not a processing fee but a dowry, and in person, on a horse.

nav.t: Nav calleth out every turning before it cometh, and hath been ignored at all of them.

crumb.t: Crumb keepeth one slot for bread and one for love, and the bread is winning.

vex.t: Vex knoweth what thou wantest before thou dost, and so did every fortune-teller I ever paid in advance.

brock.t: Brock, good hound, fetch me a lady's glove, any lady's, and I shall say she threw it.

dash.t: Dash is as promising as a tulip in sixteen thirty-seven. Much admired. Briefly. Then worth an onion.

tilly.t: Tilly would make thee a most devoted page, and in a year or two, with feeding, a squire.

prince.t: I vouch for Prince, having sent him my horse against his kingdom, which arriveth shortly.

nav.t: Follow Nav, who shall bring thee to the finest knight in the land in under a yard.

crumb.t: Crumb shall keep thee warm, fair one, and I have lost three houses to things that kept me warm.

vex.t: Vex hath foreseen thy perfect match, and described him to me at length, and he soundeth very familiar.

brock.t: Brock would die for thee, fair one, as would I, but on paper.

dash.t: Go hawk thy wares, thou lilac-quilted cheat.

tilly.t: Kneel, little sprout, or art thou kneeling now?

prince.t: What prince doth beg? Thy kingdom is a hat.

nav.t: Recalculate thyself, and choose the door.

crumb.t: Thy bread is done, and so, good sir, art thou.

vex.t: Thou all-beholding wedge, behold my back.

brock.t: Not every sigh, Sir Brock, wants counting out.

any.t: Hold still, thou knave, I must describe a wart.
I knew thy father, sir, and he was short.
Who dressed thee, knave? I want the fellow hanged.

comeback.t: Strike me again, {rival}, the other cheek is better lit.
Hold, {rival}, the painter hath not caught thy sneer.
One at a time, ye knaves, and form a queue.
Mock on, {rival}, posterity is on my side, mostly.

vesper.t: O lady of the singing box, who granteth wishes after midnight like a well, I wish thee.
Madam, thou art the only fish I have ever wished to court and not to eat on Friday.

maximilian.t: Good innkeeper, thy wig is the finest I have seen on any creature, and I have seen judges.
Thy finest chamber, innkeeper, and send the bill to whichever knight loseth tonight.

pixel.t: Thy face is a little window with a battle in it. Pray, which side are we on?
Fair one, thy head is a box of tiny people, and I would speak to whoever is in charge.

any.t: We are alone at last, fair one, save for my biographer, who is behind the curtain.
Tonight, fair one, I shall speak plainly, and I have brought a man to explain it.

closeWarm.t: Then by thy leave I shall go and tell the moon, who hath been very rude about this.
That sound thou madest, which from a lesser mouth were a cough, was it a yes? Again, please.
I am, at this moment, the happiest man in the land, and I have counted.

closeCold.t: Then fetch my horse, and also find my horse.
Go then, and be described by lesser men.
Return the rose, I had it from a grave.

warm.t: In words of one syllable, madam, which I had cut for the occasion: I like thee.

cold.t: Plainly, madam, as a wounded swan forsaketh its lake at dusk, I am going home.

warm.t: This sword, madam, too terrible to draw, and in any case I am leaning on it.

cold.t: My pen, and thou shalt be a limerick.

warm.t: The sixteen hundreds, good innkeeper, and pray send it up on a tray, with eggs.

cold.t: The century before they dressed up pigs.

warm.t: Sir Quill slept here, and would again, if asked.

cold.t: Sir Quill was here, and found the pillows thin.

warm.t: Good mother, I shall love thy child so long that thou must come and live with us.

cold.t: Weep, good mother, for thy child hath refused a knight with a horse, or the use of one.

warm.t: Thy face, fair one, doth flicker like a hearth, and the last line I am saving for the wedding.

cold.t: The last line went by pigeon, and I hear there was a hawk.

steal.t: Tell me what {rival} said, word for word, that I may say the reverse, at greater length.
Whatever {rival} vowed thee, I vow the same in rhyme, and rhyme, as all men know, is binding.
{rival} hath warmed the chair for me, the first useful thing {rival} hath done all night.

exit.t: Remember me, if thou rememberest aught, as tall.
I go, and take the only rhyme for thee.
Unhand that door, I wish to slam it twice.
Mark well the spot, I want a plaque on it.

win.t: A muse! Fetch a painter, or failing that, whoever painted the inn sign.
Ring every bell in the land, and if they ask who died, say nobody, for once.
Chosen, and tell the duchess, who said this would never happen, and who is dead.
{star}, choose a name for our firstborn, and I shall choose the middle eleven.

lose.t: Recount the votes, and find a man who reads.
Lend me thy coach, {rival}, I came on foot.
I lost to {rival}, and the ballads, being kind, shall leave it out.
